races.title: State Senate, District 24
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Brian Goldsmith
cands.bio: Small business owner, Democratic strategist and journalist. Founded two California startups, Scriber and Junction. Worked at CBS News, Yahoo News and The Atlantic. Harvard graduate with a Stanford law degree. Has not held elected office.

endorsements.text: Endorsed by Nancy Pelosi, Barbara Boxer, Hillary Clinton, State Sens. Josh Becker and Henry Stern, Assemblymembers Jesse Gabriel and Rick Chavez Zbur, former Sen. Robert Hertzberg and former LA Mayor Antonio Villaraigosa.

Endorsed by the Los Angeles Police Protective League, California Association of Highway Patrolmen, ILWU Locals 13, 63 and 94, Teamsters Joint Council 42, Everytown for Gun Safety and Moms Demand Action.

His campaign site also lists CAL FIRE, California Environmental Voters, I.A.T.S.E. Local Unions, Pete Buttigieg, District Attorney Nathan Hochman, Lt. Gov. Eleni Kounalakis and Councilmember Traci Park.

cands.gaps: We found no record of Goldsmith holding public office, so there are no official actions to report. We found nothing on his stance toward data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land purchases, abortion, school choice or teacher pay, or gun policy beyond a general mention of gun violence. His exact birthplace and the year he moved, if he did, are not stated. The campaign Issues page was cut off partway through the public safety section, so the rest of his public safety platform is not reported. We found no documented controversies or foreign ties.

qual.background: Small business owner and political consultant. Founded two tech startups. Worked as a CBS News political producer and as a Yahoo News political editor and columnist. Holds a Stanford law degree. No prior elected office.
qual.why: He has business ownership, strategy and policy-adjacent work but no legislative or local elected service, which puts him in the middle band.

back-police-order.evidence: He says he supported Prop 36 because 'the pendulum swung too far in favor of permitting lawlessness', and he opposes tolerating smash-and-grabs, property crime and violent assaults. He also says he does not want a return to mass incarceration.

workers-first.evidence: He calls the current ICE raids 'unconstitutional' and says he will stand up against what Latino Californians are facing from them.

slow-growth-protect-land.evidence: He proposes speeding up permitting, streamlining regulations and continuing to 'modernize CEQA' so housing projects are not stuck in years of review. He also proposes leasing public land that is not environmentally sensitive or in fire zones for housing.

prio.label: Matches 1 of 3 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 1 only promised

roots.summary: He says he grew up in the heart of West LA and calls himself an LA native, and he now lives in Senate District 24. He gives no exact birthplace, so this uses the raised-here score.

land_positions.quote_or_summary: He supports building more housing, including workforce, modular and mixed-income housing. He wants faster permitting, continued CEQA modernization, below-market leases of underused public land, and office-to-residential conversions. He says public land that is environmentally sensitive or in fire danger zones should be excluded.

cands.name: John M. Erickson
cands.bio: West Hollywood City Councilmember (elected 2020) and former mayor. Chief of Staff at Alliance for a Better Community and former Vice President of Planned Parenthood Los Angeles. Earlier worked as a city council intern and policy staffer. Democratic candidate for State Senate District 24.

endorsements.text: Working Families Party, California Federation of Labor Unions AFL-CIO, California Nurses Association, California Teachers Association, National Union of Healthcare Workers, California Young Democrats, Equality California and YIMBY Action, plus several Sway voter-guide groups (as listed by Ballotpedia).

cands.gaps: His birthplace, childhood home and the year he moved to California were not found. The record doesn't show whether his childhood in a town called Ripon was in Wisconsin or California. We found no documented legislative actions or sponsored bills beyond his own campaign's descriptions of his city council work. We found no stated positions on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buyers, or school vouchers and teacher pay. The campaign's "Seen the attack ads? Here are the facts" section was cut off and could not be read, so any attacks on him and his responses are not covered here. His Ballotpedia education entry was not used because of a likely error (see review note).

land.label: 1 documented position for data centers or more development

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Elected to the West Hollywood City Council in 2020 and served as mayor. Nonprofit executive (Chief of Staff, Alliance for a Better Community; VP, Planned Parenthood Los Angeles). Earlier a city council intern and policy staffer.
qual.why: Local elected office including mayor, plus policy staff and nonprofit management work, fits the middle band. He has no prior state legislative service. His campaign site says he delivered a $31 million budget surplus as mayor, but that figure is his own claim and was not independently confirmed.

pro-life.evidence: Lists protecting abortion rights and California's role as a sanctuary for reproductive care among his top policy passions.

workers-first.evidence: Says California must set an example as a sanctuary for all, and that his work protects immigrant communities.

slow-growth-protect-land.evidence: Says he will back cities that use statewide housing bonuses and incentivize approval of new housing projects, and favors streamlined permitting and rebuild processes.

back-police-order.evidence: Says he will work with first responders and support state matching grants to update fire, police and first responder stations. He also says public safety should be "smart" rather than a tough-versus-soft-on-crime debate.
